title: Quotient and reduction of an affine group torsor through a normal subgroup
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $N,G,Q$ be affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $i:N\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed normal subgroup [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] and let $q:G\to Q$ be a faithfully flat surjective homomorphism of finite presentation with scheme-theoretic kernel $i(N)$ [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume that $q$ identifies $Q$ with the fppf sheaf quotient $G/N$. For a $k$-scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and any represented right $G$-torsor $P\to S$, form the fppf sheaf quotient $P/N$ for the restricted right $N$-action; here quotient means sheafification of the orbit presheaf on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. A represented right $L$-torsor $Y\to B$ means a faithfully flat surjective map of finite presentation with a right $L$-action and isomorphism $Y\times_k L\simeq Y\times_BY$, $(y,l)\mapsto(y,yl)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $P/N$ is represented by a scheme $R$ over $S$, the induced $R\to S$ with its right $Q$-action is a $Q$-torsor, and the quotient map $P\to R$ is an $N$-torsor. For every $S$-section $a:S\to R$, the scheme $P_a=P\times_{R,a}S$ is an $N$-torsor over $S$, and any section $b:S\to P_a$ composes to a section $e:S\to P$. All these assertions are compatible with base change $S'\to S$.

source.place: Agent-extracted normal-extension reduction used in Proposition 16.55, printed p.344; Example 2.68 and Proposition 2.69, printed p.60; affine faithfully flat descent in Appendix A.80--A.81, printed pp.584--585. Arbitrary-base form of the standard torsor quotient construction.

proof.text: Put $U=P$ with cover $p:U\to S$. It is fppf by the torsor hypotheses and [def-pc-fppf-site], hence fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]. For any $T\to S$ carrying a point $u\in P(T)$, the map $G_T\to P_T$, $h\mapsto uh$, is an isomorphism: the inverse sends $x$ to the second coordinate of the inverse of the given torsor isomorphism at $(u,x)$. In particular the diagonal point over $U=P$ gives this trivialization over our cover. Pullbacks of $p$ remain flat, surjective and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3); thus they too are fppf covers. Represented functors are sheaves on these covers by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] and the fppf-to-fpqc implication.

source.place: Definition 2.66 and Example 2.67, printed p.60; arbitrary-base covering facts: Stacks Tags 021L, 022C, 01U9, 01S1, 01TS, 023Q

proof.text: The affine scheme $Q$ is flat over $k$ by [lem-pc-flat-field]. It is finitely presented over $k$: the field has just the ideals $0,k$, so its spectrum is locally Noetherian; finite type gives local finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], and affineness supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). The identity section makes $Q$ nonempty, so $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective. Consequently every projection $Q_T\to T$ is flat, surjective and finitely presented by the three base-change results of step 1. It is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1). The map $q$ is affine as well: a morphism between affine schemes is the spectrum morphism of its ring map, and over an affine open of its target it is the relative spectrum of the restricted algebra. Its base changes are therefore affine by the same result.

source.place: Proposition 2.69 and Appendix A.80, printed pp.60,584; Stacks Tags 01S7, 01SD, 01TX, 01TS, 01U9, 01S1

proof.text: The map $G\times_kN\to G\times_QG$, $(h,n)\mapsto(h,hi(n))$, has inverse $(h,h')\mapsto(h,h^{-1}h')$. The second coordinate factors through $N=\ker q$, since $q(h)^{-1}q(h')=1$; this is the fibre-product definition of kernel in [def-sc-group-scheme]. These two formulas are inverse by the group laws and the kernel identification. They are scheme morphisms by that universal property, or equivalently by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. Thus $q$ with its right $N$-action is an $N$-torsor. This calculation uses the scheme-theoretic kernel, not an assertion that $G(T)\to Q(T)$ is surjective.

source.place: Example 2.68, printed p.60, with the inverse requested in Exercise 2-1 written out

proof.text: On $U\times_SU$, let $u_0,u_1$ be the two tautological points of $P$ and let $g_{01}$ be the unique morphism to $G$ with $u_1=u_0g_{01}$, obtained from the inverse torsor isomorphism. On triple overlaps uniqueness gives $g_{02}=g_{01}g_{12}$. Give $Q_U\to U$ the transition $z\mapsto q(g_{01})^{-1}z$ from the $u_0$ chart to the $u_1$ chart. Its inverse is left multiplication by $q(g_{01})$, and $q(g_{12})^{-1}q(g_{01})^{-1}=q(g_{02})^{-1}$ proves the cocycle of [def-pd-descent-datum]. Since $Q_U\to U$ is affine and $U\to S$ is fpqc, [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] gives a scheme $R/S$ with $R_U\simeq Q_U$ and exactly these transitions. The local maps $P_U\to Q_U$, $u h\mapsto q(h)$, are compatible: coordinates change from $h$ to $g_{01}^{-1}h$. They descend to $r:P\to R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Right multiplication on $Q_U$ commutes with all these left translations, so it descends along the pullback cover of $R\times_kQ$ to a right $Q$-action. Associativity and the unit law descend as equalities by uniqueness in the same sheaf theorem.

source.place: Appendix A.81, printed p.585, affine descent applied to the explicit quotient transition datum; Stacks Tags 023V, 0245, 023Q

proof.text: The map $r$ is invariant under $N$, as is seen on $U$ from $q(hi(n))=q(h)$; equality descends by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Hence it defines a natural map $v:T\mapsto P(T)/N(T)\to h_R$. Check the two conditions of [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] on the chosen big fppf site. For $a:T\to R$, first pass to the fppf cover $T\times_SU\to T$. There $a$ is a $Q$-coordinate $z$, and the pullback of the fppf map $q:G\to Q$ along $z$ is a further fppf cover on which $z$ lifts to $h$. The point $uh$ lifts $a$. For injectivity, take $x,x'\in P(T)$ with $r(x)=r(x')$. The original torsor isomorphism gives a unique $g\in G(T)$ with $x'=xg$. On $T\times_SU$, writing $x=uh$ gives $q(h)=q(hg)$, hence $q(g)=1$. This equality holds on $T$ by representable descent. The scheme-theoretic kernel then gives $g=i(n)$ for a unique $n\in N(T)$, so $x,x'$ already have the same orbit. The local-bijection theorem therefore identifies the sheafification of the orbit presheaf with $h_R$. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] makes this identification the one induced by $r$. Thus $R$ represents precisely the quotient required in the statement.

source.place: Agent completion of the normal-extension argument behind Proposition 16.55, printed p.344; local-bijection criterion: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/LocallyBijective.lean:114--116 and :160--161, with Sites/Localization.lean:80--82 (source of lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection); not Stacks Tag 00WJ, which concerns exactness.

proof.text: Over $U$, the action map $R\times_kQ\to R\times_SR$ is $(z,t)\mapsto(z,zt)$, with inverse $(z,z')\mapsto(z,z^{-1}z')$. These local inverse maps agree on overlaps: replacing both $z,z'$ by $az,az'$ leaves $z^{-1}z'$ unchanged. Representable descent [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] glues the inverse, and its two inverse identities hold globally by uniqueness there. The map $R\to S$ is affine, flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine], [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-locally-finite-presentation], applied to its model $Q_U\to U$ on the fpqc cover $U\to S$. Affineness gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), hence finite presentation. Finally $R\to S$ is surjective: for any $s$, take $u\in U$ above it, and the identity point in the fibre of $Q_U$ over $u$ maps to a point of $R$ above $s$. These prove that $R\to S$ is a $Q$-torsor.

source.place: Proposition 2.69 and Appendix A.80, printed pp.60,584; Stacks Tags 023Q, 02L5, 02L2, 02KY, 01S7

proof.text: The pullback of $r:P\to R$ along the fppf cover $R_U\to R$ is $q_U:G_U\to Q_U$. Indeed $P_U\simeq G_U$ and $R_U\simeq Q_U$ identify $r_U$ with $q_U$ by its construction. Thus this pullback is affine, flat, surjective and finitely presented (steps 1--2). The three descent results of step 6 show that $r$ is affine, flat and locally of finite presentation, and affine permanence again gives finite presentation. Surjectivity descends directly on points: choose a point of the surjective cover $R_U\to R$ over any given point of $R$, then a point above it under the surjective $q_U$. The right $N$-action preserves $r$ by step 5. The inverse of $P\times_kN\to P\times_RP$ sends $(x,x')$ to $(x,n)$, where the inverse original $G$-torsor map gives $x'=xg$ and the equality $r(x)=r(x')$ forces $q(g)=1$ exactly as in step 5. Factor through the scheme-theoretic kernel to get $n$; these are morphisms by the kernel universal property, and the formulas are inverse. This proves that $r$ is an $N$-torsor.

source.place: Example 2.68, Proposition 2.69 and Appendix A.80, printed pp.60,584; Stacks Tags 02L5, 02L2, 02KY, 01S7

proof.text: For a section $a:S\to R$, form $P_a=P\times_{R,a}S$. Its structure map is the base change of $r$, so is flat, surjective and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The base-changed torsor isomorphism identifies $P_a\times_kN$ with $P_a\times_SP_a$ by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]; hence $P_a$ is an $N$-torsor. If $b:S\to P_a$ is a section, $e=\operatorname{pr}_P b$ satisfies $p e=\operatorname{id}_S$ because $P_a\to S$ is its structure map. Thus it is the required section of $P$.

source.place: Proposition 16.55, printed p.344, normal-extension induction; base change of Definition 2.66

proof.text: For any $S'\to S$, the pulled-back cover $U'=U\times_SS'\to S'$ is fppf (step 1). On it the models are still $G_{U'}\xrightarrow{q_{U'}}Q_{U'}$ and the transition is still $z\mapsto q(g_{01}|_{U'\times_{S'}U'})^{-1}z$. The local-lift and orbit-equality test of step 5 therefore identifies $(P\times_SS')/N$ with $h_{R\times_SS'}$. This is the canonical comparison induced by $r\times_SS'$, since both maps send the orbit of $x$ to its quotient point. Local actions and quotient maps agree in these coordinates, so they agree globally by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $(P_a)\times_SS'\simeq(P\times_SS')\times_{R\times_SS',a'}S'$; both projections of this isomorphism are the evident pulled-back projections. It consequently identifies the actions, sections and composites $\operatorname{pr}_P b$ after pullback. Identity and iterated base changes have the same projections, so uniqueness in the universal property gives their coherence. This proves all base-change assertions.
